hints: Notice the ball is moving vertically upwards and slowing down, so think about how its upward speed changes with height.
Recall that air resistance opposes the velocity and gets larger when speed is larger, so link the falling upward speed to the size of the drag force.
Add the forces with direction: weight acts downwards and drag on the way up also acts downwards, so consider what happens to $W + \text{drag}$ when drag gets smaller.
walkthrough: Identify the two vertical forces on the way up: weight $W = mg$ downwards, which is constant, and air resistance (drag) downwards because it opposes the upward velocity.
Recall that drag magnitude increases with speed. The ball decelerates as it rises because both weight and drag act against the upward motion.
Since upward speed decreases towards the top of flight, the speed-dependent air resistance decreases.
Write the magnitude of the downward resultant force as $F_{res} = W + F_{drag}$ because both forces point the same way.
As $F_{drag}$ gets smaller while $W$ stays constant, $F_{res}$ must get smaller during the upward motion.
Therefore air resistance decreases and resultant force decreases. This is option A.

options.A: Air resistance falls as upward speed falls, and $W + \text{drag}$ downwards therefore falls.
options.B: Air resistance does decrease, but the downward sum of weight plus smaller drag must decrease, not increase.
options.C: Speed decreases on the way up so drag cannot increase; the resultant also decreases rather than following an increasing drag.
options.D: Both increasing is wrong because the ball slows down, so speed-dependent drag gets smaller.
